candidates.raw_excerpt: In mid-September, a new company called Robot Entertainment Kombat hosted what it claimed was the first-ever human-on-robot cage fight in California. candidates.title: Satlyt Secures $8M in Seed Financing
candidates.raw_excerpt: Satlyt has been boosted by securing $8 million in seed financing led by non sibi ventures . The funding will accelerate development of its virtual Al data centers in space, expand its engineering and customer delivery teams, and scale software deployments across spacecraft operated by other companies. The company announced the successful seed funding, Oct. 1. Satlyt moves more processing onto the spacecraft itself, reducing the need to send every raw image or system log to Earth for analysis. That can reduce communications demands and the wait for useful results. The company’s approach is to make computing hardware on existing spacecraft more useful through software. Operators can process data closer to where it is collected, while application developers gain a way to run their software in orbit. Over time, Satlyt aims to give spacecraft from different operators a shared software layer for coordinating computing resources. The next planned deployment is expected to support two applications on one spacecraft: research software and a commercial imagery-processing application. “Running applications on existing spacecraft gives operators a way to do more with the computing hardware they already have in orbit. Our job is to make those applications practical to deploy and operate. This financing lets us expand the engineering and delivery teams needed to support more spacecraft and customers, while building toward computing resources that can work together across missions,” Rama Afullo, founder and CEO of Satlyt, said in a statement.   The post Satlyt Secures $8M in Seed Financing appeared first on Via Satellite .

candidates.raw_excerpt: Canada Rocket Company (CRC) will build Canada’s first large-scale rocket engine test facility at London International Airport, a $30 million complex intended for static firing of the company’s methalox engines as it develops a reusable medium-lift launch vehicle. The Jeremy Hansen Test Facility is named for Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen, the first Canadian to fly around the Moon. CRC will lease 50 acres from the Greater London International Airport Authority for an engine test area and a 12,000-square-foot office and shop building used for engineering, assembly, and test preparation. Putting the shop next to the stands is meant to keep engine build-up, instrumentation, and test ops in one place rather than splitting that work across distant sites. The test area is planned for up to three vertical and horizontal stands, with the ability to static-fire engines producing more than 1 MN of thrust. Vertical stands are typically used for flight-like firings. Horizontal stands are often used earlier in a campaign for access, instrumentation, and engine development work. candidates.title: Miller Tapped to Head SPACECOM, Oversee Move To Huntsville
candidates.raw_excerpt: The White House on Tuesday nominated U.S. Space Force Lt. Gen. David Miller for his fourth star as the head of U.S. Space Command (SPACECOM). Miller would replace Gen. Stephen Whiting as SPACECOM commander. Since last November, Miller has served as the deputy chief of space operations for strategy, plans, programs and requirements. Before that, Miller was the final head of Space Operations Command (SpOC). Last November, Space Force changed SpOC’s name to Combat Forces Command (CFC) to signal a move “toward enhanced combat readiness and integrated space defense.” CFC’s legacy dates back to Air Force Space Command, which became SpOC in October 2020. In September last year, Miller spoke of the first space electromagnetic warfare tactical operations center and coming advances in space control, orbital warfare , and the surveillance, tracking, and targeting of potential adversary air and space systems — a foreshadowing of Air Force Secretary Troy Meink’s statement on the existence of U.S. orbital weapons at the Air & Space Forces Association’s conference this month. If confirmed by the Senate as head of SPACECOM, Miller will have oversight of the command’s move from Peterson Space Force Base, Colorado, to Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama — a move that was the subject of a bitter partisan battle on Capitol Hill. candidates.title: Trusted Computing Group Creates Key New Working Group Focusing on Aerospace Security
candidates.raw_excerpt: The Trusted Computing Group (TCG) has created a new Aerospace and Non-Terrestrial Systems Solutions Working Group (AERO-SWG) as it looks to play a key role in keeping satellite systems secure. Focusing on satellite networks, unmanned systems, autonomous platforms, and disconnected edge environments, AERO-SWG will aim to help operators apply trusted computing principles to strengthen the resilience and integrity of the systems now central to global communications and critical infrastructure. TCG announced the new group, Sept. 29. AERO-SWG will aim to establish trust within the devices, platforms, gateways, and supply chains that underpin the global communications, defense, transportation, and critical infrastructure society now relies upon. This will be achieved through practical guidance, gap analysis, and recommendations to existing TCG Work Groups. The group will be chaired by TCG member Thorsten Stremlau of Nvidia. AERO-SWG will explore how layered hardware and firmware security can be applied across aircraft, satellites and ground stations to strengthen trust at the platform level. This includes Trusted Platform Modile (TPM)-based Roots-of-Trust for flight-critical software, Device Identifier Composition Engine (DICE) for lightweight subsystem protection, and CyRes for restoring corrupted firmware in flight or in orbit. “AERO-SWG gives the industry a dedicated forum to ensure trusted computing in the toughest aerospace environments, including satellites and autonomous systems. By bringing experts together to focus on practical needs and real deployment barriers, the group will help accelerate the development of secure and interoperable technologies in this crucial sector,” Joe Pennisi, president of TCG, said in a statement. candidates.title: FCC Continues Deregulation Push with Environmental Regulations and More Spectrum
candidates.raw_excerpt: The FCC continued its push to deregulate and open up new spectrum with two major decisions on Wednesday — exempting space activities from certain federal environmental regulations and opening up 1,000 megahertz of spectrum. The FCC voted to modernize its approach to National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) regulations, including clarifying space-based operations including launch, deploymentment, and operating spacecraft are not classified as major federal actions requiring NEPA review. It also clarifies that spectrum authorizations and sites like satellite Earth stations also are not major federal actions. “In taking this approach, we avoid constraining American innovation, commerce, and U.S. leadership in space by applying NEPA’s terrestrial regulatory regime to this orbital domain,” FCC Commissioner Olivia Trusty said during the FCC meeting. “To be clear, this clarification does not create a regulatory vacuum for space operations or diminish U.S. treaty obligations. U.S. licensed operators remain subject to requirements addressing orbital debris and space safety, where, among other things, collision mitigation and congestion issues can be addressed,” Trusty added. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in his statement that the intent of these changes is to speed up wireless and broadband deployment and remove the “unpredictable specter of activist lawsuits or last-minute surprises” from next-generation space development like direct-to-device systems and orbital data centers. candidates.title: New Jersey So Flooded That a Shark Was Spotted Swimming Through a Suburban Neighborhood
candidates.raw_excerpt: A shark has been spotted wandering the streets of New Jersey. And it ain’t here for the vig , either. With the powerful nor’easter storm battering the Eastern Seaboard over the weekend, floodwaters have poured into the perhaps unfortunately named town of Surf City, turning its suburban streets into aquatic thoroughfares. Marine traffic obliged. In a viral video taken Saturday by a local resident, a shark — as in the fish, not the mobsters who enforce usurious loans— is seen swimming through the town like it owns the place. The shark’s dorsal fin, in cinematic fashion, even breaks through the surface of the water. “Is that a little shark?” one person can be heard saying, almost in disbelief. “It’s coming this way!” Fortunately, this is almost certainly no man-eater. According to Greg Skomal, a white shark researcher with the Massachusetts Division of Marine Fisheries, the shark in the video appears to be a smooth dogfish — “which is a very small, harmless shark that is common in those waters,” he told ABC News . After patrolling the resident’s driveway, the shark reportedly started swimming toward Barnegat Bay, according to ABC , seemingly content with making its presence known. A snowless nor’easter over the weekend has ravaged parts of the east coast, with New Jersey and New York among the hardest hit states, where both governors have declared states of emergency for specific locales.  Strong winds exceeding 60 miles per hour knocked trees over, killing a 56-year-old man in Brooklyn. Flooding was reported all over New Jersey, seeping into resident’s homes. On the more lighthearted side of things, many an opportunistic kayaker has pounced on the chance to traverse their towns on narrow boats. An entire 19th century shipwreck was even unearthed by the storm. And now sharks, apparently, are enjoying the sightseeing occasion of a lifetime.
